answer: Keep the two accessioned core segments as two persistent specimens; do not merge them into a single new identity. CIDOC CRM's E19 Physical Object scope note itself says that what counts as one complete documented item versus its parts/components 'may be purely administrative or may be a result of the order in which the item was acquired' -- CRM does not treat this as a fact of nature to be corrected once discovered, it treats it as a documentation decision already made 50 years ago by each field crew. That decision was used to build decades of loan paperwork citing the two separate accession numbers, and CRM's Monotonicity principle (Modelling principles > Monotonicity) holds that later, better knowledge must add to a description, not retract a correctly-made earlier one -- so retiring or merging the two accession identifiers would violate Monotonicity and break, not honour, the old citations. Concretely: model each core segment as its own persistent item -- E19 Physical Object at the base-CRM level, or, better fitted to a geological-survey bore core, S11 Amount of Matter / S13 Sample in CRMsci, whose own scope notes give 'the sequence of layers of a bore core' as a worked example of an identity criterion that survives splitting and physical separation. Each keeps its original P1/P48 identifier (both properties are many-valued and explicitly designed to accumulate identifiers over time without displacing earlier ones), so the loan records referencing the old numbers remain valid without any change. The stratigrapher's new claim -- that the bottom of one core is the physically continuous extension of the top of the other -- should be recorded as a new, attributed, revisable assertion linking the two existing specimens, using the standard CRM idiom for exactly this: an E13 Attribute Assignment (carried out by the stratigrapher) with P140 assigned attribute to / P141 assigned linking the two segments and P177 assigned property of type naming the relationship, rather than any structural part-whole property. I could not find a purpose-built CRM property for 'was originally one continuous body, now permanently separated' -- and neither, apparently, could the CRM SIG: in thread t1080 (HW S11, 2018) Martin Doerr raises this exact bore-core-splitting case and concludes 'we need to think about the identity and unity criteria. Probably we need a transitive property of its own,' and the scope note was left revised but the transitive property was never created (S11's dossier lists this thread as its only debate, still unresolved). So the honest position is: CRM fully supports keeping the two specimens separate and documenting the physical/geological correlation as an opinion, but there is a genuine, acknowledged gap for expressing that correlation as a first-class relation.

rejected_alternatives.option: P46 is composed of / forms part of
rejected_alternatives.why_not: P46's own FOL declares P46(x,y) => P132(x,y) (spatiotemporal overlap) and requires the part to be currently, spatially contained in the whole. The two segments have sat in separate repository buildings for fifty years -- they are not co-located, so the 'whole' P46 presupposes does not exist. connect E19 E19 and connect S11 S11 both surface P46 as an option, but it does not fit a claim about matter that is not physically rejoined.

L54 is a 'non-unique identification' link for co-referencing duplicate records of what is asserted to be the same entity. The two core segments are not the same object under any description -- they are two distinct extracted pieces of rock -- so this is the wrong relation even though connect offered it for both E19-E19 and S11-S11.

rejected_alternatives.option: Merge into a single new specimen record, retiring the two old accession numbers
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Violates the Monotonicity principle: the separate-specimen classification was correctly made and has been used continuously in loan documentation for 50 years; new knowledge should be added on top of it, not used to retract it.

This is CRM's actual built-in property for documenting a physical relationship between two units, which made it tempting, but its domain/range is A8 Stratigraphic Unit -> A8 Stratigraphic Unit -- in-situ excavation/deposit contexts observed at a site, not portable specimens sitting in accessioned boxes in two different buildings. It models the relationship between strata at the borehole locations, not between the two extracted core objects.

rejected_alternatives.option: S24 Sample Splitting event (via O27 split / O29 removed sub-sample)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: This CRMsci mechanism models a single, deliberate splitting activity that produces a tracked sub-sample from a known original at the time of splitting. Our case is the reverse: two specimens were independently created and accessioned without either crew knowing about the other, and the relationship is a retrospective geological inference decades later, not a witnessed splitting event. (Note: `concept S24` itself returned 'No such concept' in this tool -- the class is only visible here as the domain of O27/O29.)

notes: concept S24 (CRMsci Sample Splitting) errored with 'No such concept' even though it appears as the domain of O27/O29 -- could not inspect its own scope note directly. `docs` only indexes the base CRM 7.3.2 spec, so it returned nothing useful for CRMsci-specific terms ('Sample Splitting'); all CRMsci/CRMarchaeo material had to come through `concept`. `quote` does not accept a concept id (E19) as a source -- it only checks threads/messages/document chunks, so the E19 scope-note wording is cited as a plain identifier, not a verified quote. The core theoretical gap -- no dedicated CRM property for 'two independently-accessioned specimens later found to have been one continuous natural body' -- is well evidenced (thread t1080) but genuinely unresolved in the standard, which is why confidence is medium rather than high.
